title: The Pre-Season Outlay: Why a Sporting Club or Academy Pays Months Before a Member Signs Up
linkedin:
A cricket academy, swim school or netball club right now is paying for a season that hasn't started yet.

Coaches booked. Pool or ground hire locked in. Uniforms and equipment ordered. All invoiced or paid in the weeks before a single session runs.

The membership fees that cover it move at a completely different pace, often in instalments spread across the term, sometimes trickling in well after enrolment officially opens.

Here's the part that catches even experienced operators: growth makes this worse, not better. A bigger season needs another coach, another hired court, a larger equipment order, and all of that scales with the capacity being added, not with how fast new members pay. The costs land in the same tight window they always have. The fees still arrive on the same slow schedule.

A club that grows meaningfully from one season to the next can walk into its busiest month feeling tighter on cash than the smaller season before it, even though the eventual profit is stronger.

The fix isn't collecting fees upfront or growing slower. It's mapping the season week by week rather than as one annual total, so the pinch point between the invoice and the instalment is visible before it arrives, not discovered in real time.

Full piece on the ProfitPulse blog.

If you run a cricket academy, swim school, netball club or any season based sporting business along the east coast, you are probably locking in coaches, facility hire and equipment orders right now for the summer season ahead.

Here's the pattern we see every year with clubs and academies in this position. The costs of running the season, coaching fees, ground or pool hire, insurance, equipment, are mostly committed before the first session runs. The membership and term fees that pay for all of it arrive on a slower, staggered schedule, often across instalments through the term. That gap is normal. It still catches experienced operators every year, especially in a season that is growing, because a bigger enrolment needs more coaching and facility capacity committed up front, not just more fees landing eventually.

The fix isn't rushing families to pay upfront. It's mapping the season week by week so the pinch point between cost and collection is visible well before it arrives, rather than showing up as a surprise in the bank balance.

If you run a seasonal club, academy or membership business and want a clearer read on your own timing before the next season locks in, read the full piece on the ProfitPulse blog.
